bottleneck: Natural AAV serotypes have broad tropism: AAV9 crosses the blood-brain barrier but also transduces liver, heart, and spleen. When the target is specific neurons or retinal cells, off-target transduction wastes dose, lowers efficacy at the intended site, and risks toxicity from expressing potent genes in the wrong tissues. More cells exposed also means more viral antigen presented to the immune system.
current_state: Capsid engineering via directed evolution is producing more selective variants, but no vector yet achieves surgical single-cell-type specificity in humans. Tissue-specific promoters help only partially.

sources.title: Cracking the AAV Code: Engineering Precision

title: Broad AAV tropism causes off-target transduction
why_it_blocks: Imprecision forces higher systemic doses to reach the target, which drives dose-limiting hepatotoxicity and immune engagement. Until delivery is targeted, potent genetic payloads remain too dangerous for many indications.
